jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
在遵循合规和工作程序的条件下，开展以临床为导向的销售行为，提供符合临床的产品解决方案，开发医疗机构及分销商，完成年度指标任务。
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world. tex

Job Description
角色与职责
- Roles & Responsibility

- 1.Formulate annual, quarterly and monthly sales plan, track sales target completion, adjust sales strategies timely to achieve assigned revenue and market share goals.

- 2.Maintain long term stable cooperation with hospital clinical departments, equipment procurement offices and distribution partners, organize product demonstrations, clinical trial communication and technical exchange meetings of ultrasound systems.

- 3. Cooperate with application specialists and after sales engineers to deliver pre sale technical support and post sale customer follow up, resolve customer equipment usage problems and maintain customer satisfaction.
4. Complete regular sales report, market analysis document and customer file management as required by company internal management rules.

- Qualification/Requirements

- 1. Hold full time college diploma or above, major in clinical medicine, biomedical engineering, medical instrument marketing or other related medical fields is preferred.
2. Possess more than two years working experience in medical imaging equipment sales, with existing customer resources of hospital ultrasound department or medical distribution channels in Northeast China region.
3. Master basic professional knowledge of ultrasound diagnostic equipment, understand hospital medical equipment procurement process and tender bidding procedures.
4. Have independent business negotiation ability, can take regular business trips within the responsible region.
5. Skilled in written and oral English for daily business communication and document reading.
6. Abide by company compliance policies, with no bad record of sales compliance violation.

- Desired Characteristics

- 1. Strong market insight and active initiative in business development, able to take pressure from sales target assessment.
2. Good cross department communication and coordination ability, capable of cooperating with technical, marketing and after sales teams to deliver integrated customer solutions.
3. Patient and rigorous communication attitude, good at establishing trust relationships with clinical doctors and hospital management staff.
4. Strong learning ability to quickly master new ultrasound product technologies, clinical application advantages and industry policy changes.

jobs.title: Strategic Sourcing Leader - NPI
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Strategic Sourcing Leader – NPI is responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies that support the successful launch of new products from concept through commercialization. This role partners closely with Engineering, Product Management, Quality, Operations, and Suppliers to ensure component availability, cost competitiveness, supply continuity, and scalability throughout the product development lifecycle.

The leader drives supplier selection, risk assessment, contract negotiations, and should-cost analysis while aligning sourcing decisions with business objectives, quality requirements, and regulatory standards. The position plays a critical role in achieving program milestones by proactively managing supply chain risks and identifying opportunities for cost reduction, value engineering, and supplier innovation.

GE Healthcare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description
Job Responsibilities:
- Develop and implement comprehensive strategic sourcing plans for all NPI programs, aligning with OEC Medical Systems' product roadmaps and business objectives.

- Lead the identification, evaluation, and selection of new suppliers for critical NPI components and services, conducting thorough risk assessments and due diligence.

- Negotiate favorable terms, conditions, and pricing with suppliers, establishing robust contracts that support NPI timelines and cost targets.

- Collaborate closely with R&D, Engineering, Quality, and Operations teams throughout the NPI lifecycle to ensure seamless integration of supplier capabilities and materials.

- Manage supplier relationships, driving performance improvement, innovation, and risk mitigation for NPI-related suppliers.

- Implement early supplier involvement programs to leverage supplier expertise in design for manufacturability and cost optimization.

- Develop and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for NPI sourcing activities, reporting on progress and identifying areas for continuous improvement.

- Stay abreast of market trends, technological advancements, and supplier capabilities within the medical device industry.

- Drive cost reduction initiatives and value engineering activities for NPI components and sub-assemblies.

Required Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.

- Minimum of 3 years of experience in strategic sourcing, or procurement with a significant focus on New Product Introduction (NPI) within a highly regulated industry, preferably medical devices OR GEHC OMLP grad.

- Experience with successful supplier identification, negotiation, and management for complex NPI projects.

- Excellent negotiation, communication, and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across all levels of the organization and with external partners.

- Experience developing and executing strategic sourcing plans that deliver measurable results.

- Proficiency in ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle) and e-sourcing tools.

- Experience analyzing and interpreting data to make informed decisions.

- Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

- Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required. (10-20%)

jobs.title: Executive Heartbeat Lean Leader, Office of Heartbeat
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
Based in Europe, this executive role leads the enterprise-wide Lean transformation within GE HealthCare’s Office of Heartbeat. It supports the development, deployment, and sustained alignment of the Heartbeat Business System with the company’s 2030 goals.

Transformation Leadership: The role champions, coaches, and mentors Lean change; leads Heartbeat Lean Leaders; partners with stakeholders to prioritize improvement opportunities; and co-leads operating reviews, strategy, and priority planning across regions, segments, and functions.

Business System Deployment: Responsibilities include supporting bootcamps, coaching, and training while embedding standard work, daily management, problem solving, kaizen, value stream mapping, and action planning into business operations. The position also builds Lean capability and manages the organizational change required to sustain these practices.

Operational Impact: By analyzing work at the genba, diagnosing challenges, testing improvements, and executing Hoshin Kanri priorities, the role is expected to improve business results and culture, strengthen leadership capability, and contribute to improved EBITDA and Free Cash Flow.

Required Profile: Candidates need a bachelor’s degree, at least 15 years of general management or Lean operational leadership experience, and at least 10 years of Lean capability-building experience. The profile also calls for regulated-industry knowledge, experience with AI-enabled tools, global Lean-system deployment, strong facilitation and program-management skills, executive communication, accountability, commercial focus, and change-management expertise, preferably using the ADKAR framework.

Job Description
Your Challenge
The Executive Lean Leader is responsible for supporting the design, adoption, functional leadership, and execution of the enterprise-wide Lean transformation within the Office of Heartbeat at GE HealthCare. As a key member of the Office of Heartbeat team, the Executive Lean Leader contributes to the overall strategy of how we run, change, and act in the business, guided by the principles and processes of the Heartbeat Business System (HBS).

This role is critical to ensure the Heartbeat Business System is developed, deployed, and sustained in direct alignment with the company’s 2030 goals. The Executive Lean Leader will lead impactful operating routines and drive execution of critical projects. The role is based in Europe.

Your Responsibilities
Our Heartbeat Business System is based on Lean thinking and practices and will be an integral part of the way we run, change, and act in our business for the long-term. Each Executive Lean Leader contributes to this progression within the organization.

The Executive Lean Leader will focus on selecting, supporting, and assisting with the improvement efforts tied to the Office of Heartbeat’s most critical business processes (e.g., Hoshin Kanri), primarily in the innovation (STO), commercial, integrated supply chain, service, and functional areas. By analyzing work at the genba with our people, diagnosing our challenges, and testing process improvements through an action plan, the Executive Lean Leader will demonstrate continuous improvement and breakthrough performance — ultimately shaping the company culture and brand.

The goal is to positively impact results and culture by establishing standards, institutionalizing daily management processes, adopting consistent problem-solving methods, and executing on Hoshin Kanri priorities. As a key member of the Office of Heartbeat team, the Executive Lean Leader will help strengthen and develop the evolving Heartbeat Business System and build people and leader capability in the Heartbeat fundamentals — standard work, daily management system, problem solving, kaizen, value stream mapping, and action planning — with a growth mindset that enables culture change. This will require significant change management to embed effectively throughout the organization.

Expectations
Lean Leadership & Transformation
- Provide overall Lean leadership at the appropriate Region / Segment / Function level and drive the Lean transformation by serving as a champion, coach, and mentor for change
- Lead and mentor the Region / Segment / Function teams of Heartbeat Lean Leaders across the organization
- Partner with global business stakeholders across segments and regions to identify, prioritize, and execute improvement opportunities through Kaizen events and Lean initiatives
- Co-lead Region / Segment / Function operating rhythms (operating reviews, long-term strategy, priorities planning) in partnership with subject-matter experts and senior leaders

Heartbeat Business System Deployment
- Support the development and activities of the Heartbeat Business System, including bootcamps, leader coaching, and training on Heartbeat fundamentals
- Install the Heartbeat behaviors and fundamentals into how we run the business: standard work, daily management system, problem solving, kaizen, value stream mapping, and action planning

Capability Building
- Establish a Lean capability program that ensures the application of globally recognized standards for Lean principles and practices, serves as a benchmark for achievement, and provides a common roadmap for continuous improvement and people development
- Develop capability across the spectrum — from the tactical (deployment and application of principles, concepts, and methods) to the strategic (a transformation that deeply impacts a key value stream) — with effective change management

Leadership, Culture, & Change Management
- Demonstrate and commit to servant leadership and partnership with peers and leaders
- Align behaviors and practices to our shared Cultural Operating Principles and Heartbeat Behaviors
- Development and deployment of the Heartbeat Business System will result in improved EBITDA and Free Cash Flow

Your Experience
- BS or BA Degree; Master’s Degree preferred
- Minimum 15 years of experience in a General Management or Lean/operational leadership role
- Minimum 10 years of capability building across a variety of Lean practices, including Hoshin Kanri, problem solving, daily management system, standard work, and value stream mapping
- Working knowledge of business processes within the medical equipment or other regulated industry
- Experience leveraging AI-enabled tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or similar platforms to accelerate the way work is done, and continuously learning new ways of using emerging technologies
- Ability to travel up to 40% across Europe and internationally.

Desired Characteristics
- Ideally built and/or designed an organizational management system
- Ideally developed the playbook for the core processes of an organizational business system
- Demonstrated successful leadership and proficiency in installing and sustaining a Lean system for a global organization with operations and services teams
- Deep, hands-on experience with Lean principles and practices; credible with practitioners and executives alike
- Ability to accurately assess key business metrics and situations from a general manager’s or executive leader’s perspective
- Excellent time, program, and project management skills — brings order and structure quickly to initiatives and other critical, high-visibility programs
- Strong facilitation and ability to influence without authority across segments, regions, and functions
- High attention to detail in daily and visual management without losing the strategic thread
- Proven ability to hold senior leaders accountable to commitments with candor and respect
- Growth mindset with hands-on approach; comfortable at the genba and in the boardroom
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive storytelling
- Experience with Change Management (preferably the ADKAR framework)
- Deep commercial experience with a focus on the customer and end-user experience

Job Description Summary
The Europe Service Finance Analyst provides operational Finance support to the Europe Service organization, with a focus on financial reporting, data analysis, forecasting, and performance monitoring.
Reporting to the Europe Service Finance Manager, the role works closely with zone and local Finance teams, Service Operations, Commercial teams, and Controllership to ensure accurate and timely financial information.
This is a hands-on role responsible for maintaining reports, analyzing variances, supporting planning cycles, and monitoring key Service performance indicators. The position is suited to an early-career Finance professional looking to develop strong FP&A and business-partnering capabilities in a European and matrixed environment.

Job Description
Key Responsibilities
- Prepare and maintain weekly and monthly Service financial reports and dashboards.
- Collect, consolidate, and validate financial data from European zones and local teams.
- Support month-end and quarter-end closing activities, including accruals, reclassifications, and variance analysis.
- Monitor Service revenue, gross margin, operating expenses, productivity, backlog, contract performance, and other relevant KPIs.
- Analyze actual results against budget, forecast, prior year, and business targets.
- Identify reporting inconsistencies, investigate variances, and follow up with local Finance and operational teams.

- Maintain accurate documentation, reporting calendars, and process instructions.

- Approximately one to three years of experience in Finance, FP&A, accounting, reporting, audit, or business analysis; relevant internship experience may also be considered.

jobs.title: PCS Finance Manager Europe
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The PCS Finance Manager Europe is accountable for Product Finance activities across the PCS segment for the Europe Zone. Reporting to the FP&A Manager Europe, the role combines financial planning, data analysis, business partnering, and reporting to support business decisions and deliver sustainable, profitable growth within the segment.

The role works closely with the LCT PCS General Managers to drive correct capital-allocation decisions, go-to-market strategy, product positioning, and NPI launches, and is accountable for accurate forecasting and planning of orders, sales, and overall profitability for the PCS segment at Europe level. It ensures clear dialogue and linkage with the Global Markets PCS Finance Manager and the Global Markets PCS GM.

Acting as a trusted finance business partner, the manager supports the FP&A vision for Europe – contributing to an insight-led finance function and driving the adoption of AI and automation across the PCS finance activities, at both LCT and Central levels, to transform how the segment plans, forecasts, and reports.

Job Description
PCS Product Finance & Business Partnering
- Partner with LCT PCS General Managers to drive operating performance and act as champion for strategic initiatives within the segment, including capital-allocation decisions, go-to-market strategy, product positioning, and NPI launches.

- Own accurate forecasting and planning of orders, sales, and overall profitability for the PCS segment at Europe level.

- Partner with commercial and service organizations to lay-out growth strategies and execution plans that meet financial goals.

- Work horizontally across the zone to ensure consistency and best-practice sharing within the PCS segment.

- Coordinate with the Global Markets PCS segment finance team to ensure alignment and activation plan on strategy, provide visibility on execution and performance, and secure the support needed, in clear linkage with the Global Markets PCS Finance Manager and GM.

Financial Planning, Reporting & Analysis
- Actively participate in the formulation and analysis of financial plans – budgets, forecasts, and strategic plans – ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and market conditions

- Coordinate with the zone finance teams to provide centralized finance reporting capabilities, commercial and operational productivity metrics, and forecasting that contribute to overall business growth.

- Provide financial direction to establish and accomplish functional and operational financial goals and objectives.

- Collect, process, and analyze financial data to discern patterns, forecast future trends, and provide decision-makers with actionable insights

- Establish and maintain a financial measurement and reporting system that provides management with appropriate information and counsel.

- Drive operating forecasts and plans, including appropriate contingency planning.

- Craft insightful financial reports and presentations for senior management, clearly delineating performance, highlighting variances versus targets, and explaining underlying drivers with precision and clarity

- The role provides the Europe LCT teams the forecasting and budgeting outputs based on accurate modeling and incorporating the LCT com finance analysts' inputs

- Vigilantly monitor financial performance against benchmarks, identify significant variances, conduct root-cause analysis, and provide incisive recommendations to optimize performance and mitigate risks.

- Undertake in-depth financial evaluations of proposed projects or initiatives, scrutinizing their impact on the organization’s financial health, profitability, and strategic trajectory, and provide recommendations to guide decision-making.

- Support productivity initiatives, to drive outcomes to deliver measurable value across the zone.

- Understand and support to drive actions in relation to costs (direct and indirect) on financial goals and measurements.

Process Improvement, AI & Transformation
- Support the FP&A vision for Europe, positioning the PCS finance function as an insight-led, predictive, and value-adding business partner rather than a purely reporting-oriented team.

- Drive the adoption of AI and automation to accelerate planning, forecasting, reporting, and analysis while improving accuracy and consistency.

- Identify and scale high-impact use cases (e.g., AI-assisted forecasting, automated variance analysis, self-service reporting) and embed them into standard processes and governance, ensuring responsible and compliant use in line with GE HealthCare policies.

Qualifications
Education & Experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or another numeracy-based discipline, and 5+ years of financial work experience.

- Strong knowledge of GE HealthCare’s financial, commercial, and service operating systems.

- Strong financial and accounting background, with detailed knowledge of the Healthcare industry and market.

- In-depth understanding of the segment’s product development and launch (NPI) processes, with advanced analytical skills.

Financial Acumen & Analysis
- Ability to manage and interpret financial data and product metrics.

- Excellent skills in cost and profit evaluation and analysis.

- Ability to make strategic decisions and provide strategic guidance to the business.

Technical & Data Proficiency
- Excellent command of MS Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint), with advanced Excel skills.

- Familiarity with Business Intelligence tools (e.g., Power BI) and ERP systems (SAP preferred).

- Exposure to AI and automation in a finance context (e.g., generative AI, machine-learning-based forecasting, RPA, or advanced analytics), with a demonstrated appetite to identify use cases and drive adoption across teams.

Key Competencies
- Effective communicator with the ability to lead numerous and diverse teams and to convey complex business issues clearly and concisely.

- Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to influence others and drive change while working across all levels, functions, and zones.

- Strong critical thinking skills and ability to add value to operating teams.

- Experience leading in a matrixed environment.

- Adaptable and flexible: open to change in response to new information, different or unexpected circumstances, and comfortable operating in ambiguous situations.

Languages
- Fluent in English.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Senior Program Manager - Ultrasound Probes will lead complex, cross-functional programs across the global Probes organization. This role spans the full Probes portfolio and will work closely with Probes segment leaders, who serve as Product Managers, to translate business and portfolio priorities into disciplined execution.

The Senior Program Manager will drive strategic and operational initiatives across R&D, Product Management, Supply Chain, QARA, Manufacturing, Service, and Regions. Key areas of focus include complex NPI programs, Hoshin Kanri deployment, operating rhythm improvements, and embedding the HeartBeat operating principle into NPIs and other cross-functional programs.

This role requires a strong operational leader who can bring structure to complexity, align diverse stakeholders, manage multiple workstreams and swimlanes, and drive execution with rigor and transparency.

GE Healthcare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator, operating at the center of an ecosystem working toward precision health. Our Ultrasound business provides clinicians and healthcare systems with advanced ultrasound tools that deliver quality images, improved efficiency, and enhanced patient care.

The Ultrasound Probes organization plays a critical role in enabling differentiated imaging performance, clinical confidence, and product reliability across GE HealthCare's ultrasound portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership & Execution
- Lead complex, cross-functional programs across the Ultrasound Probes organization, including NPIs, portfolio priorities, operational initiatives, and strategic deployment activities.
- Translate business priorities into clear program plans with defined scope, milestones, owners, deliverables, risks, and decision points.
- Manage multiple workstreams and swimlanes, ensuring strong execution discipline, timely escalation, and clear accountability.
- Establish and maintain program governance, dashboards, operating rhythms, and leadership review mechanisms.

Partnership with Segment Leaders / Product Managers
- Work closely with Probes segment leaders / Product Managers to align program execution with portfolio strategy, customer needs, product roadmaps, and business priorities.
- Support prioritization, trade-off discussions, resource alignment, and decision-making across segments and functions.
- Ensure product and segment priorities are translated into executable plans across R&D, Supply Chain, QARA, Manufacturing, Service, and Regions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
- Serve as a key integrator across R&D, Product Management, Supply Chain, QARA, Manufacturing, Service, Finance, and regional teams.
- Facilitate alignment across global stakeholders, ensuring objectives, risks, dependencies, and decisions are clearly understood.
- Influence without direct authority in a global matrix environment.

Hoshin Kanri, HeartBeat & Operating Rhythm
- Support deployment of Hoshin Kanri priorities across the Probes organization by translating strategic objectives into measurable action plans and governance routines.
- Embed the HeartBeat operating principle into NPI and cross-functional program execution.
- Drive standard work, disciplined operating mechanisms, transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement across program teams.

Risk Management & Compliance
- Identify program risks, interdependencies, resource constraints, and execution barriers.
- Lead mitigation planning, escalation, and countermeasure execution.
- Ensure programs are executed in alignment with applicable quality, regulatory, and product development requirements in a medical device environment.

Stakeholder Communication
- Provide concise, data-driven updates to senior leadership and key stakeholders.
- Develop program dashboards, milestone reviews, risk summaries, and decision documents.
- Communicate complex issues clearly, including options, trade-offs, recommendations, and required decisions.

Qualifications & Experience

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Business, Operations, or related discipline.

- Significant experience in program management, project management, operations, product development, or business execution in a medical device, healthcare technology, life sciences, or similarly regulated industry.

- Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional, multi-site programs with multiple workstreams and stakeholders.

- Strong operational skillset, including program governance, milestone management, risk management, escalation, prioritization, and execution tracking.

- Experience working across functions such as R&D, Product Management, Quality, Regulatory, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Service, Finance, and Commercial/Regional teams.

- Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.

- Proven ability to influence without direct authority in a global matrix organization.

Desired Characteristics
- Advanced degree such as MBA, MSc, or equivalent experience.
- Program management certification or training such as PMP, Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, or equivalent.
- Experience with medical device product development, design controls, design transfer, regulatory submissions, manufacturing readiness, or post-market support.
- Experience with ultrasound, imaging systems, probes, transducers, or related healthcare technologies.
- Experience with Hoshin Kanri, strategy deployment, operating rhythms, Lean management, or enterprise transformation.
- Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
- Strong problem-solving mindset, with the ability to bring clarity, structure, and momentum in complex environments.

jobs.title: EE LCT Commercial Finance Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The EE LCT Commercial Finance Analyst acts as the financial gatekeeper for the EE LCT, responsible for financial planning, data analysis, and reporting to support commercial business decisions within the zone. The role ensures accurate financial reporting, clear oversight of P&L performance, and effective monitoring of key financial KPIs, and owns the monthly and quarterly Equipment P&L closing processes as well as the execution of the LCT budget and forecast.

Working closely with the LCT Finance Manager, local commercial finance, Controllership, and operations, the analyst provides clear visibility on financial performance and drives corrective-action resolution when required. The role supports the Europe FP&A / Product team throughout the forecasting and budgeting processes by providing timely inputs to improve forecast accuracy and by highlighting key risks and opportunities. The position reports directly to the LCT Finance Manager, with dotted-line reporting to the Europe FP&A Leader.

As a driver of digitalization, the analyst leverages Power BI, Power Query, SQL, Excel, and AI capabilities to automate reporting and simplify business and finance processes, supporting the FP&A vision for Europe and the adoption of AI and automation at both LCT and Central levels to improve the speed, reliability, and transparency of financial information.

Job Description
Responsibilities
P&L Ownership & Financial Reporting
- Own the monthly and quarterly Equipment P&L closing processes, ensuring accurate entries and reporting while delivering clear performance analysis across segments and costs versus Forecast, Budget, and Prior Year.
- Own the order and sales reconciliation reviews in collaboration with the relevant commercial and operational teams.
- Own key financial KPI tracking and provide timely visibility to LCT leadership.
- Own local financial reporting needs and drive the streamlining of reporting processes.
- Craft articulate and insightful financial reports and presentations for senior management, highlighting variances versus targets and elucidating underlying drivers with precision and clarity.

​
Planning, Forecasting & Analysis
- Support the LCT Finance Manager in operationalizing and executing the LCT budget and forecast, while providing the Europe FP&A team with business inputs and insights on monthly and quarterly financial results.
- Actively participate in the formulation and analysis of financial plans – budgets, forecasts, and strategic plans – ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and market conditions.
- Engage in the comprehensive collection, processing, and analysis of financial data to discern patterns, forecast future trends, and furnish decision-makers with actionable insights.
- Vigilantly monitor financial performance against predefined benchmarks, identify significant variances, conduct root-cause analyses, and furnish incisive recommendations to optimize performance and mitigate risks.
- Undertake in-depth financial evaluations of proposed projects or initiatives, scrutinizing their potential impact on the organization’s financial health, profitability, and strategic trajectory, and provide cogent recommendations to guide decision-making.

Business Partnering & Productivity

​
Process Improvement, AI & Digitalization
- Leverage Power BI, Power Query, SQL, Excel, and AI capabilities to automate reporting and simplify business and finance processes.
- Collaborate with other LCT Finance Analysts and the Europe FP&A team to standardize, simplify, and streamline finance processes across the business.
- Identify and scale high-impact AI and automation use cases, embedding them into standard processes and governance in line with GE HealthCare policies.

​
Qualifications
Education & Experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or another numeracy-based discipline, with confirmed financial work experience.
- Proven professional experience in finance
- Strong knowledge of GE HealthCare’s financial, commercial, and service operating systems.
- Strong financial and accounting background, with the ability to manage and interpret financial data.

​
Financial Acumen & Analysis
- Budgeting and Forecasting: proficiency in creating accurate budgets and forecasts.
- Variance Analysis: ability to analyze deviations from expected financial performance.
- Scenario Modeling: capability to model different financial scenarios.

​
Technical & Data Proficiency
- Advanced Excel skills: mastery of functions, pivot tables, look-up functions, filtering, conditional formatting, and consolidation functions.
- Business Intelligence tools (e.g., Power BI): creating interactive dashboards, reports, and visualizations for stakeholders, with familiarity in Power Query and SQL.

- Exposure to AI and automation in a finance context (e.g., generative AI, machine-learning-based forecasting, RPA, or advanced analytics), with a demonstrated appetite to identify use cases and drive adoption across teams.

Key Competencies

jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager (f/m/d) - AIS
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Supply Chain Program Manager (f/m/d) - AIS handles planning, coordinating, and executing supplier transfer programs to ensure seamless transitions into current production/sites, minimize risks, and maintain business continuity. The role requires collaboration with global cross-functional teams, suppliers, and stakeholders to ensure quality cost and timeline objectives are met.

At GE HealthCare, our machines, our software, our solutions, our services, and our people make a genuine difference to medical professionals and patients all over the world. That’s because we never lose sight of what healthcare really needs—the human touch.

Job Description
Roles & Responsibilities:

Project Planning & execution

- Develop and manage comprehensive project plans for supplier & manufacturing transfers including timelines, budgets, and resource allocations.
- Define project scope, objectives, and deliverables in alignment with business goal.
- Coordinate cross-functional teams including sourcing, engineering, quality, operations, QA and Regulatory.
- Monitor and track project progress, identifying and mitigating risks and issues throughout the lifecycle of the program.
- Lead regular project meetings, reporting status and providing regular updates to stakeholders and leadership teams.
- Ensure compliance to GEHC QMS and industry standards.
- Work closely with suppliers to ensure smooth transition, including knowledge transfer, validation and capability/ readiness assessments.

Risk Management & Compliance

- Identify risks associated with supplier & manufacturing transfers and develop mitigation strategies with the program team.
- Ensure adherence to regulatory requirements including GEHC QMS standards and international medical device regulations and quality standards (ISO 13485, FDA 21 CFR Part 820, EU MDR, China NMPA, Japan PMDA) and other industry best practices.
- Conduct risk assessments (DFMEA, PFMEA) and implement contingency plans to prevent disruptions/ impacts to the program’s deliverables.
- Work with regulatory and quality teams to maintain documentation and approvals required for compliance.

Cost and Performance Management:

- Manage project budgets, ensuring cost efficiency while meeting performance goals.
- Optimize supply chain strategies to reduce costs, improve efficiency and maintain product quality.
- Track supplier performance post-transfer/implementation, identifying corrective actions if necessary to ensure long-term supplier sustainability.

Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business Management or related field.
- 8+ years of project management experience in supplier transfer, supply chain or manufacturing, preferably in the medical device industry.
- Experience managing global program teams and working across different time zones, cultures and regulatory landscapes.
- Experience in regulated industries such as medical devices, pharmaceuticals, aerospace, automotive.
- Strong knowledge of medical device manufacturing processes, validation and quality systems.
- Strong project management skills with experience in tools like MS Project and/or Smartsheet.
- Knowledge of supplier qualifications, validations and risk management.
- Strong problem-solving, negotiation and communication skills with the ability to work effectively across different cultures and time zones.
- Ability to manage multiple programs in parallel.
- PMP, Six Sigma, and/or Lean Manufacturing certification is a plus.

What we offer

- We offer a role specific compensation and a competitive salary and fringe benefit package reflecting your profile and experience.
- In Austria we are required to state the minimum pay. For this position, the annual compensation package starts at € 80.000. We will be pleased to discuss the appropriate effective salary based on your qualifications and experience.
- An exciting and diverse range of responsibilities in a growth-oriented company
- An interdisciplinary team and an international work environment
- Flextime and flexible working hours
- Free electric charging stations and ample parking facilities on the company premises
- An additional day off for your birthday
- Convenient public transportation access with a complimentary company shuttle to the Redl-Zipf train station, located 2 km away

If you are interested in learning more we are looking forward to your online-application!
Don't meet all the requirements? We are aware that there is almost never a perfect profile. You can learn (almost) anything as long as you are interested and enjoy new topics and challenges. In short: we look forward to receiving your application, even if you do not yet meet the requirements 100%!

About us
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator with over 100 years of healthcare industry experience and around 50,000 employees globally. We enable clinicians to make faster, more informed decisions through intelligent devices, data analytics, applications and services, supported by our Edison intelligence platform. We operate at the center of an ecosystem working toward precision health - digitizing healthcare, helping drive productivity and improving outcomes for patients, providers, health systems and researchers around the world.
Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. jobs.title: Senior Sourcing Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
As a Global Sourcing Leader, you will be part of a team responsible for $205M global semiconductor spend for both tier 1 and tier 2 supply base in addition to supporting our Strategic Business Units within the electronic component category.

GE Healthcare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description
Roles and Responsibilities
Category Strategy & Supplier Management
- Develop and execute sourcing strategy for active components (semiconductors, ICs, FPGAs, power devices, memory).
- Optimize supplier base, drive dual/multi-sourcing, and manage supplier segmentation.
- Align supplier roadmaps with technology evolution, NPI, and lifecycle requirements.

Commercial Leadership & Negotiations
- Lead strategic negotiations with key suppliers (pricing, contracts, capacity, terms).
- Execute RFQ/RFP processes and allocate business based on cost, capability, and risk.
- Drive cost productivity, payment terms improvements, and contract coverage.

Supply Continuity & Risk Management
- Ensure continuity of supply through proactive risk assessment (capacity, allocation, geopolitical risks).
- Develop mitigation strategies including alternate sourcing, buffering, and supplier diversification.
- Manage supplier escalations, claims, and recovery actions.

Lifecycle & Obsolescence Management
- Lead PCN/EOL management, last-time-buy strategies, and lifecycle risk mitigation.
- Partner with Component Engineering to reduce legacy dependency and improve product longevity.

Value Engineering & Cost Optimization
- Drive VA/VE, redesign initiatives, and should-cost modeling.
- Enable alternate component qualification and platforming opportunities for cost reduction.
- Deliver measurable cost savings through cross-functional execution.

Market Intelligence & Analytics
- Provide insights on pricing trends, lead times, and supply-demand dynamics.
- Use data analytics to support sourcing decisions and cost forecasting Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Collaborate with Engineering, SBUs, Quality, EMS, and Program Management teams.
- Support NPI programs, redesign initiatives, and compliance requirements.
- Drive alignment across global stakeholders to ensure execution excellence.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s Degree in Electronics Engineering with Supply Chain or related field
- 4+ years of experience in sourcing electronic components / semiconductors
- Proven experience in supplier management, negotiations, and strategy deployment
- Strong business and financial acumen

Desired Characteristics
- Deep domain expertise in active components (ICs, semiconductors, power devices, memory)
- Strong understanding of component lifecycle, obsolescence, and alternate sourcing
- Proven ability to build and manage long-term strategic supplier relationships
- Strong influencing, communication, and stakeholder management skills
- Experience working in global, cross-functional environments
- Project/program management experience with measurable outcomes

Business Impact
- Direct impact on cost, supply continuity, and product lifecycle for a multi-million-dollar electronics portfolio
- Key contributor to supplier strategy, innovation alignment, and business continuity in a volatile semiconductor market
